extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, recommenders, and data/script editors participating in PCI Evolutionary Biology preprint evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for submitting, reviewing, and recommending evolutionary-biology preprints on the PCI Evolutionary Biology platform, including editorial expectations, scope, ethics, and data/script requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scientific, methodological, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evolutionary Biology recommends only preprints that meet high scientific, methodological, and ethical standards regardless of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform's recommendation is contingent on the work satisfying rigorous standards in scientific quality, methodology, and ethics rather than perceived impact. This is the overarching acceptance principle that guides selection and recommendation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory sharing of data, code, and analysis scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires authors to share data, code, and analysis scripts with reviewers upon submission and with readers after recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide the materials necessary for verifying results to reviewers at submission; upon positive recommendation these materials must be made available to readers. This requirement supports reproducibility and transparency during peer review and after recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of sample sizes in empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Expects clear justification of sample sizes in empirical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical submissions should explicitly justify sample size choices (e.g., power analyses, sampling rationale). This is part of the methodological standards reviewers will consider when assessing rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming replications, preregistered research, and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes replications, preregistered research, and negative results as valid contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform explicitly values and encourages submissions that improve scientific robustness such as replication studies, preregistered protocols, and well-reported negative or null results; these are not disfavored by impact considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest policy for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not accept submissions with financial conflicts of interest; other conflicts must be minimal and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose conflicts. Financial conflicts of interest are a bar to acceptance; non-financial conflicts should be minimized and transparently declared. This applies to authorship and submission-level disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest avoidance for reviewers and recommenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensures, as much as possible, that reviewers and recommenders are free from conflicts of interest related to the study or its authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform takes steps to appoint reviewers and recommenders without conflicts related to the work or authors. Where conflicts exist they should be declared and managed; impartiality of evaluators is a stated expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender-interest prerequisite for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Only preprints that attract the interest of at least one recommender are sent for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preprint must first attract at least one recommender (akin to an associate editor) who selects it for review based on their interest. Recommenders choose work that 'stands out' for its context, questions, methods, or findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for recommender interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted preprints that do not attract the interest of a recommender within a period of 20 days are not considered for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no recommender expresses interest within 20 days of submission the preprint will not proceed to peer review under PCI Evolutionary Biology. This is a procedural gate tied to recommender selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders select work that stands out (to them) for its context, questions, methods, or findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection by recommenders is based on perceived distinctiveness or merit in one or more dimensions: relevance/context, research questions, methodological approach, or the significance/robustness of findings. This is a qualitative filter prior to formal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of accepted topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Will evaluate preprints dealing with all fields of Evolutionary Biology, with an explicit list of subjects (e.g., Adaptation, Behavior & Social Evolution, Bioinformatics & Computational Biology, Evo‑Devo, Evolutionary Applications, Evolutionary Dynamics, Evolutionary Ecology, Evolutionary Epidemiology, Evolutionary Theory, Experimental Evolution, Expression Studies, Genetic conflicts, Genome Evolution, Genotype‑Phenotype, Human Evolution, Hybridization/Introgression, Life History, Macroevolution, Molecular Evolution, Morphological Evolution, Non Genetic Inheritance, Paleontology, Phenotypic Plasticity, Phylogenetics/Phylogenomics, Phylogeography & Biogeography, Population Genetics/Genomics, Quantitative Genetics, Reproduction and Sex, Sexual Selection, Speciation, Species interactions, Systematics/Taxonomy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative and indicates a broad remit across evolutionary biology subfields. Authors should ensure their topic fits within these domains when considering submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted study types and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints may describe empirical or theoretical studies and be based on observations from experiments or nature, or previously acquired data; may report results of verbal, computer, or mathematical models; studies of methodologies are appreciated; perspectives, reviews, opinions and comments on previously published articles are also welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform accepts a wide variety of study types: empirical, theoretical, modeling, methods papers, reviews, perspectives, opinions, and comments. Authors should present appropriate methodological detail for the type (e.g., models should include assumptions and code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to COPE and platform code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Community In subscribes to the principles of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and has its own code of conduct that its users must comply with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants (authors, reviewers, recommenders, editors) are expected to follow COPE principles and the platform's code of conduct, which govern ethical behavior, handling of misconduct, and professional norms during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness and equity commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is attentive to equity and inclusion at all stages of the scientific article evaluation process and focuses on bringing more underrepresented people among authors and recruiting reviewers, recommenders, and Managing Board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete tools and recommendations include: the possibility to submit articles anonymously; transparency in evaluation; Managing Board consideration of underrepresentation when appointing recommenders; template messages to recommenders and reviewers that include recommendations about equity and inclusiveness; the possibility to review anonymously. PCI is also a signatory of the Coalition for Diversity and Inclusion in Scholarly Communication (C4DISC). These measures are intended to increase diversity in participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and script editorial checks using SORTEE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Data & script editors check that data and scripts are findable, reusable, and that reported results are computationally reproducible; PCI Evolutionary Biology implements the SORTEE guidelines (stages 1-6) for these checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named team of data editors performs checks focused on FAIR‑like properties and computational reproducibility following SORTEE stages 1–6. Authors should expect these checks and prepare data/scripts accordingly (clear organization, metadata, reproducible code, and instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public recommendation as citable validation
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of positive evaluation, PCI validates and publicly recommends peer-reviewed preprints, providing citable documentation for the preprint's methodological rigour and the legitimacy of its results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive outcome yields a public recommendation document that can be cited and used when submitting to journals; this serves as formal attestation of review and methodological scrutiny. Authors may then transfer the recommended preprint to the Peer Community Journal or submit it to PCI-friendly or other journals.
